ee:2016:q1.title: GATE EE 2016 | Set 1 | Question: 1
ee:2016:q1.question: The maximum value attained by the function $f(x) = x(x- 1)(x - 2)$ in the interval [1, 2] is _____.

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} f(x) &=x^3-3x^2+2x \\ f'(x)&=3x^2-6x+2\\ f'(x)&=0 \;\text{for stationary point} \end{aligned}$$

stationary points are $1+\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$

only $1+\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$ lies in [1,2]

$$\begin{aligned} f(1) &=0 \\ f(2)&=0 \\ f\left ( 1+\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \right )&=-\frac{2}{3\sqrt{3}} \end{aligned}$$

Maximum value is 0.

Therefore, the correct answer is **0**.

ee:2016:q7.title: GATE EE 2016 | Set 1 | Question: 7
ee:2016:q7.question: The phase cross-over frequency of the transfer function $G(s)=\frac{100}{(s+3)^{3}}$ in rad/s is

detailed_solution.markdown:
$G(s)=\frac{100}{(s+1)^3}$

$G(j\omega )=\frac{100}{(1+j\omega )^3}$

$\;\;=\frac{100}{1+(j\omega )^3+3(j\omega )^2+3j\omega }$

$\;\;=\frac{100}{(1-3\omega^2 )+j(3\omega-\omega^3)}$

$\;\;=\frac{100[(1-3\omega^2 )+j\omega(3-\omega^2)^2]}{[ (1-3\omega^2 )+\omega^2(3-\omega^2)^2]}$

For phase corssover frequency $\omega_{ph} Img[G(j \omega )]=0;$

Hence, $\omega (3-\omega ^2)=0$

$\omega =0; \pm \sqrt{3}$

Therefore, $\omega _{ph}=\sqrt{3}$ rad/sec

Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

ee:2016:q8.title: GATE EE 2016 | Set 1 | Question: 8
ee:2016:q8.question:
Consider a continuous-time system with input x(t) and output y(t) given by

y(t) = x(t) cos(t)

This system is

detailed_solution.concept: Signals and Systems - Linear Time Invariant Systems
detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} y(t)&=x(t)\cos (t)\\ &\text{To check linearity,}\\ y_1(t)&=x_1(t)\cos (t)\\ &[y_1(t) \text{ is output for }x_1(t)]\\ y_2(t)&=x_2(t) \cos (t)\\ &[y_2(t) \text{ is output for }x_2(t)]\\ \text{so, the}& \text{ output for }(x_1(t)+ x_2(t)) \text{ will be}\\ y(t)&=[x_1(t)+ x_2(t)]\cos (t)\\ &=y_1(t)+y_2(t) \end{aligned}$$

So, the system is linear, to check time invariance.

The delayed output,

$y(t-t_0)=x(t-t_0)\cos (t-t_0)$

The output for delayed input,

$y(t, t_0)=x(t-t_0)\cos (t)$

Since,  $y(t-t_0)\neq y(t,t_0)$

System is time varying.

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

ee:2016:q14.title: GATE EE 2016 | Set 1 | Question: 14
ee:2016:q14.question: A soft-iron toroid is concentric with a long straight conductor carrying a direct current I. If the relative permeability $\mu _r$ of soft-iron is 100, the ratio of the magnetic flux densities at two adjacent points located just inside and just outside the toroid, is _______.

detailed_solution.markdown:
Toroid has field,

$$\begin{aligned} B &\propto \mu \\ As\;\; \mu &=100 \;(\text{inside field}) \end{aligned}$$

Magnetic field density B at any point at a distance at r is

$$\begin{aligned} B &=\frac{\mu I}{2 \pi r} \\ Now\;\;B_{at\; r^-}&=\frac{\mu_0 \mu_r I}{2 \pi r^-}\;(\text{just inside toroid})\\ Now\;\;B_{at\; r^+}&=\frac{\mu_0 I}{2 \pi r^+}\;(\text{just outside toroid})\\ \frac{B_{at\; r^-}}{B_{at\; r^+}}&=\mu _r=100 \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **100** (acceptable range: [99, 101]).

ee:2016:q20.title: GATE EE 2016 | Set 1 | Question: 20
ee:2016:q20.question:
The magnitude of three-phase fault currents at buses A and B of a power system are 10 pu and 8 pu,
respectively. Neglect all resistances in the system and consider the pre-fault system to be unloaded.
The pre-fault voltage at all buses in the system is 1.0 pu. The voltage magnitude at bus B during a three-phase fault at bus A is 0.8 pu. The voltage magnitude at bus A during a three-phase fault at bus B, in pu, is ________.

detailed_solution.markdown:
Voltage at bus B after 3-phase fault at A=0.8 p.u.

$$\begin{aligned} V_B &=V_{(prefault)}-Z_{12} \times I_{f(A)} \\ 0.8&= 1.0-Z_{12} \times 10 \\ Z_{12} &=0.02 p.u. \\ V_A &=V_{(prefault)}-Z_{12}I_{f(B)} \\ V_A&=1.0-(0.02 \times 8) \\ &= 0.84p.u. \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **0.84** (acceptable range: [0.83, 0.85]).

ee:2016:q26.title: GATE EE 2016 | Set 1 | Question: 26
ee:2016:q26.question: Candidates were asked to come to an interview with 3 pens each. Black, blue, green and red were the permitted pen colours that the candidate could bring. The probability that a candidate comes with all 3 pens having the same colour is _____.

detailed_solution.markdown:
- **Concept / Subtopic**: Engineering Mathematics (EE) - Combinatorics with Repetition & Discrete Probability
- **Given Parameters**:
  - Number of pens selected: $r = 3$.
  - Number of distinct permitted pen colors: $n = 4$ (Black, Blue, Green, Red).
  - Target event: A candidate arrives with all 3 pens having the same color.
- **Governing Equations**:
  - The combination of pens a candidate brings constitutes an unordered multiset of size $r$ chosen from $n$ distinct categories with repetition allowed.
  - The total number of distinct color combinations is given by the stars-and-bars multiset coefficient:
    $$N_{\text{total}} = \binom{n + r - 1}{r} = \binom{4 + 3 - 1}{3} = \binom{6}{3}$$
- **Step-by-Step Analytical Derivation**:
  1. **Compute Total Distinct Combinations**:
     $$\binom{6}{3} = \frac{6 \times 5 \times 4}{3 \times 2 \times 1} = 20$$
  2. **Compute Favorable Outcomes (All Same Color)**:
     - The candidate can bring all 3 pens of the same color in exactly 4 ways:
       1. $\{3\text{ Black}\}$
       2. $\{3\text{ Blue}\}$
       3. $\{3\text{ Green}\}$
       4. $\{3\text{ Red}\}$
     - Number of favorable combinations: $N_{\text{favorable}} = 4$.
  3. **Calculate Probability**:
     - Assuming all distinct combinations of 3 pens are equally likely:
       $$P(\text{all 3 pens same color}) = \frac{N_{\text{favorable}}}{N_{\text{total}}} = \frac{4}{20} = \frac{1}{5} = 0.2$$

Therefore, the correct numerical value is **0.2**.

ee:2016:q27.title: GATE EE 2016 | Set 1 | Question: 27
ee:2016:q27.question: Let $S=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty }n\alpha ^{n} \; where \;  |\alpha | \lt 1$. The value of $\alpha$ in the range $0 \lt \alpha \lt 1$, such that $S= 2\alpha$  is _______.

detailed_solution.markdown:
The Z-transform of

$$\begin{aligned} \alpha ^n u(n)&\rightarrow \frac{1}{(1-\alpha Z^{-1})}\\ n\alpha ^n u(n)&\rightarrow \frac{\alpha Z^{-1}}{(1-\alpha Z^{-1})^2}\\ \frac{\alpha Z^{-1}}{(1-\alpha Z^{-1})^2}&=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty }n\alpha ^nZ^{-n} \end{aligned}$$

If we put Z=1 in above equation, we get,

$$\begin{aligned} \frac{\alpha }{(1-\alpha )^2}&=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty }n\alpha ^n\\ \text{Since, }\sum_{n=0}^{\infty }n\alpha ^n&=2\alpha =\frac{\alpha }{(1-\alpha )^2}\\ \text{So,}2&=\frac{1}{(1-\alpha )^2}\\ \Rightarrow \;\;\alpha &=0.29 \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **0.295** (acceptable range: [0.28, 0.31]).

ee:2016:q29.title: GATE EE 2016 | Set 1 | Question: 29
ee:2016:q29.question: Let A be a 4 x 3 real matrix with rank 2. Which one of the following statement is TRUE?
options: Rank of $A^{T} A$ is less than 2.
Rank of $A^{T} A$ is equal to 2.
Rank of $A^{T} A$ is greater than 2.
Rank of $A^{T} A$ can be any number between 1 and 3.

detailed_solution.markdown:
- **Concept / Subtopic**: Engineering Mathematics (EE) - Linear Algebra & Gram Matrix Rank Invariance
- **Given Parameters**:
  - Matrix $A$ is a real matrix of size $4 \times 3$.
  - Given rank of $A$: $\text{rank}(A) = 2$.
- **Governing Theorem (Gram Matrix Nullspace Property)**:
  - For any real matrix $A \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times n}$, the null space of $A$ and the null space of $A^T A$ are identical:
    $$\text{Null}(A^T A) = \text{Null}(A)$$
- **Proof of Nullspace Equality**:
  1. If $\mathbf{x} \in \text{Null}(A)$, then $A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{0}$. Multiplying by $A^T$ gives $A^T A \mathbf{x} = A^T \mathbf{0} = \mathbf{0}$, so $\mathbf{x} \in \text{Null}(A^T A)$.
  2. Conversely, if $\mathbf{x} \in \text{Null}(A^T A)$, then $(A^T A)\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{0}$. Pre-multiplying by $\mathbf{x}^T$ yields:
     $$\mathbf{x}^T (A^T A) \mathbf{x} = (A\mathbf{x})^T (A\mathbf{x}) = \|A\mathbf{x}\|^2 = 0 \implies A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{0}$$
     Thus, $\mathbf{x} \in \text{Null}(A)$.
  - Therefore, $\text{Null}(A^T A) = \text{Null}(A)$, which means:
    $$\text{nullity}(A^T A) = \text{nullity}(A)$$
- **Step-by-Step Analytical Derivation**:
  - Both $A$ and $A^T A$ have $n = 3$ columns.
  - By the Rank-Nullity Theorem:
    $$\text{rank}(A) + \text{nullity}(A) = 3$$
    $$\text{rank}(A^T A) + \text{nullity}(A^T A) = 3$$
  - Equating the two expressions:
    $$\text{rank}(A^T A) = \text{rank}(A)$$
  - Since $\text{rank}(A) = 2$:
    $$\text{rank}(A^T A) = 2$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option B (Rank of $A^{T} A$ is equal to 2.)**.

ee:2016:q31.question:
Consider the following state-space representation of a linear time-invariant system.
$$\dot{x}(t)=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0\\ 0&2 \end{bmatrix}x(t),$$ $y(t)=c^{T}x(t),$ $$c=\begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 1 \end{bmatrix}$$ and $$x(0)=\begin{bmatrix} 1\\ 1 \end{bmatrix}$$
The value of y(t) for $t= log_{e}2$ is______.

detailed_solution.concept: Signals and Systems - Linear Time Invariant Systems
detailed_solution.markdown:
- **Concept / Subtopic**: Signals and Systems / Control Systems - State Transition Matrix & Output Response
- **Given State Space Model**:
  $$\dot{\mathbf{x}}(t) = A \mathbf{x}(t), \quad A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$$
  $$y(t) = \mathbf{c}^T \mathbf{x}(t), \quad \mathbf{c} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}$$
  $$\mathbf{x}(0) = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}$$
  Target evaluation time: $t = \ln(2)$.
- **Governing Equations**:
  - For a diagonal system matrix $A = \text{diag}(\lambda_1, \lambda_2)$, the state transition matrix $\Phi(t) = e^{At}$ is directly:
    $$e^{At} = \begin{bmatrix} e^{\lambda_1 t} & 0 \\ 0 & e^{\lambda_2 t} \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} e^t & 0 \\ 0 & e^{2t} \end{bmatrix}$$
  - The zero-input state response is:
    $$\mathbf{x}(t) = e^{At} \mathbf{x}(0)$$
  - The system scalar output is:
    $$y(t) = \mathbf{c}^T \mathbf{x}(t) = \mathbf{c}^T e^{At} \mathbf{x}(0)$$
- **Step-by-Step Analytical Derivation**:
  1. **Compute State Vector $\mathbf{x}(t)$**:
     $$\mathbf{x}(t) = \begin{bmatrix} e^t & 0 \\ 0 & e^{2t} \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} e^t \\ e^{2t} \end{bmatrix}$$
  2. **Compute Scalar Output $y(t)$**:
     $$y(t) = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} e^t \\ e^{2t} \end{bmatrix} = e^t + e^{2t}$$
  3. **Evaluate at $t = \ln(2)$**:
     $$e^t = e^{\ln(2)} = 2$$
     $$e^{2t} = \left(e^{\ln(2)}\right)^2 = 2^2 = 4$$
     $$y(\ln 2) = 2 + 4 = 6$$

Therefore, the correct numerical value is **6**.

ee:2016:q32.title: GATE EE 2016 | Set 1 | Question: 32
ee:2016:q32.question: Loop transfer function of a feedback system is $G(s)H(s)=\frac{s+3}{s^{2}(s-3)}$. Take the Nyquist contour in the clockwise direction. Then, the Nyquist plot of G(s)H(s) encircles -1+ j0

detailed_solution.markdown: Nyquist plot of $G(s)H(s)=\frac{s+3}{s^2(s-3)}$ is as shown below From the Nyquist plot G(s)H(s) encircle -1+j0 once in clockwise direction. Alternate Solution: Characteristic equation, $1+G(s)H(s)=0$ $s^2(s-3)+(s+3)=0$ $s^3-3s^2+s+3=0$ using Routh's array $$\left.\begin{matrix} s^3\\ s^2\\ s^1\\ s \end{matrix}\right|\begin{matrix} 1 &1 \\ -3& 3\\ 2& 0\\ 3& \end{matrix}$$ There are two sign changes, hence two poles in right side of s-plane exist. $Z=2, \; P=1$ $N=P-Z=-1$ One encirclement in clockwise direction. Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

ee:2016:q33.title: GATE EE 2016 | Set 1 | Question: 33
ee:2016:q33.question:
Given the following polynomial equation $s^{3}+5.5s^{2}+8.5s+3=0$,
the number of roots of the polynomial, which have real parts strictly less than -1, is ________ .

detailed_solution.markdown: $s^3+5.5s^2+8.5s+3=0$ Putting, $s=s_1-1$ $(s_1-1)^3+5.5(s_1-1)^2+(8.5)(s_1-1)+3=0$ $s_1^3+2.5s_1^2+0.5s_1-1=1$ As there is one sign change, hence, two roots of given polynomial will lie to the left of $s=-1$. Therefore, the correct answer is **2**.

ee:2016:q34.title: GATE EE 2016 | Set 1 | Question: 34
ee:2016:q34.question:
Suppose $x_{1}(t) \; and \; x_{2}(t)$ have the Fourier transforms as shown below.

Which one of the following statements is TRUE?
options: $x_{1}(t) \; and \; x_{2}(t)$ are complex and $x_{1}(t) x_{2}(t)$ is also complex with nonzero imaginary part
$x_{1}(t) \; and \; x_{2}(t)$ are real and $x_{1}(t) x_{2}(t)$ is also real
$x_{1}(t) \; and \; x_{2}(t)$ are complex but $x_{1}(t) x_{2}(t)$ is real
$x_{1}(t) \; and \; x_{2}(t)$ are imaginary but $x_{1}(t) x_{2}(t)$ is real

detailed_solution.markdown:
By observing $X_1(j \omega )$ and $X_2(j \omega )$, we can say that they are not conjugate symmetric. Since, the fourier transform is not conjugate symmetric the signal will not be real. So, $x_1(t), x_2(t)$ are not real. Now the fourier transform of $x_1(t) \cdot x_2(t)$ will be $\frac{1}{2\pi}X_1(j \omega )*X_2(j \omega )$ and by looking at $X_1(j \omega )$ and $X_2(j \omega )$, we can say that $X_1(j \omega ) *X_2(j \omega )$ will be conjugate symmetric and thus $x_1(t) \cdot x_2(t)$ will be real.

By observing $X_1(j \omega )$ and $X_2(j \omega )$, we can say,

$X_2( \omega )=X_1(- \omega )\overset{IFT}{\rightarrow}x_2(t)=x_1(-t)\;\;...(i)$

Now, $X_1(j \omega )$ is real. Therefore, $x_1(t)$ will be conjugate symmetric.

$$\begin{aligned} \text{i.e., } x_1(t)&=x_1^*(-t) \\ \downarrow t&= -t\\ x_1(-t)&= x_1^*(t)\\ \text{Now, }x_1(t)\cdot x_2(t) &= x_1(t)\cdot x_1(-t) \;\;(from \;(i))\\ &= x_1(t)\cdot x_1^*(t)\\ &= |x_1(t)|^2=\text{real function} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

ee:2016:q35.title: GATE EE 2016 | Set 1 | Question: 35
ee:2016:q35.question:
The output of a continuous-time, linear time-invariant system is denoted by T{x(t)} where x(t) is the input signal. A signal z(t) is called eigen-signal of the system T, when $T\{z(t)\} =  \gamma z(t)$,
where $\gamma$ is a complex number, in general, and is called an eigenvalue of T. Suppose the impulse response of the system T is real and even. Which of the following statements is TRUE?
options: cos(t) is an eigen-signal but sin(t) is not
cos(t) and sin(t) are both eigen-signals but with different eigenvalues
sin(t) is an eigen-signal but cos(t) is not
cos(t) and sin(t) are both eigen-signals with identical eigenvalues

detailed_solution.concept: Signals and Systems - Linear Time Invariant Systems
detailed_solution.markdown: Given that impulse response is real and even, Thus $H(j\omega )$ will also be real and even. Since, $H(j\omega )$ is real and even thus, $H(j\omega )=H(-j\omega )$ Now, $\cos (t)$ is input i.e. $\frac{e^{jt}+e^{-jt}}{2}$ is input Output will be $\frac{H(j1)e^{jt}+H(-j1)e^{-jt}}{2}=H(j1)\left ( \frac{e^{jt}+e^{-jt}}{2} \right )= H(j1) \cos (t)$ If, $\sin (t)$ is input i.e. $\frac{e^{jt}+e^{-jt}}{2}$ is input Output will be $\frac{H(j1)e^{jt}+H(-j1)e^{-jt}}{2}=H(j1)\left ( \frac{e^{jt}-e^{-jt}}{2j} \right )= H(j1) \sin (t)$ So, $\sin (t)$ and $\cos (t)$ are eigen signal with same eigen values. Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

ee:2016:q37.title: GATE EE 2016 | Set 1 | Question: 37
ee:2016:q37.question: A 2-bit flash Analog to Digital Converter (ADC) is given below. The input is $0 \leq V_{IN} \leq 3$ Volts. The expression for the LSB of the output $B_0$ as a Boolean function of $X_{2},X_{1} \; and \; X_{0}$ is

detailed_solution.markdown: The input to digital circuuit is $X_2,X_1,X_0$ and output is $B_1,B_0$ $B_0=\bar{X_2}\bar{X_1}X_0+X_2X_1X_0$ $\;\;=X_0(\bar{X_2}\bar{X_1}+X_2X_1)$ $\;\;=X_0(\overline{X_2\oplus X_1})$ Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

ee:2016:q38.title: GATE EE 2016 | Set 1 | Question: 38
ee:2016:q38.question: Two electric charges q and -2q are placed at (0,0) and (6,0) on the x-y plane. The equation of the zero equipotential curve in the x-y plane is

detailed_solution.markdown:
Charge, Q is located at (0,0) and $-2\theta$ is located at (6,0).

To find V at any point $(x,y)$

$$\begin{aligned} V_Q &= \frac{Q}{4 \pi \in \sqrt{x^2+y^2}}\\ V_{-2Q}&=\frac{-2Q}{4 \pi \in (\sqrt{(x-6)^2 +y^2})} \\ V_{total}&=0 \\ &= \frac{Q}{4 \pi \in \sqrt{x^2+y^2}} \\ & +\frac{-2Q}{4 \pi \in (\sqrt{(x-6)^2 +y^2})} \\ \sqrt{(x-6)^2 +y^2}&=2(\sqrt{x^2+y^2}) \\ x^2+36-12x+y^2&=4x^2+4y^2 \\ 3x^2+3y^2+12x&=36 \\ x^2+y^2+4x&=12 \\ (x+2)^2+y^2&=16 \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

ee:2016:q39.question: In the circuit shown, switch $S_2$ has been closed for a long time. At time t=0 switch $S_1$ is closed. At $t = 0^{+}$, the rate of change of current through the inductor, in amperes per second, is _____.

detailed_solution.concept: Electric Circuits - Transients and Steady State Response
detailed_solution.markdown: KCL at node A, $\frac{V_A-3}{1}+\frac{3}{2}+\frac{V_A-3}{2}=0$ $2(V_A-3)+3+(V_A-3)=0$ $3V_A=6$ $V_A=2$ $V_A=L\frac{di(0^+)}{dt}=2$ $\frac{di(0^+)}{dt}=\frac{2}{L}=\frac{2}{1}=2A/sec$ Therefore, the correct answer is **2** (acceptable range: [1.9, 2.1]).

ee:2016:q40.title: GATE EE 2016 | Set 1 | Question: 40
ee:2016:q40.question:
A three-phase cable is supplying 800 kW and 600 kVAr to an inductive load. It is intended to supply an additional resistive load of 100 kW through the same cable without increasing the heat
dissipation in the cable, by providing a three-phase bank of capacitors connected in star across the load. Given the line voltage is 3.3 kV, 50 Hz, the capacitance per phase of the bank, expressed in microfarads, is ________.

detailed_solution.concept: Power Systems - Distribution Systems, Cables and Insulators
detailed_solution.markdown:
$\text{KVA}_1=\sqrt{800^2+600^2}=100 \text{ KVA}$

Without excessive heat dissipation means current should be constant (i.e.) KVA erating must be constatn.

In second case active power,

P=800+100=900 KW

Reactive power in second case,

$Q_2=\sqrt{1000^2-900^2}=435.889 \text{ KVAR}$

Reactive power supplied by the three phase bank = 600-435.889 =164.44 KVAR

$$\begin{aligned} Q_{bank}/ph&=\frac{164.11}{3}=54.7 \text{ KVAR} \\ V/ph&= \frac{3.3}{\sqrt{3}}=1.9051 \text{ KV}\\ Q_c/ph&=\frac{(V/ph)^2}{X_C} \\ X_C&=\frac{(1.9052 \times 10^3)^2}{54.7 \times 10^3} \\ &= 66.36\; W\\ C&= \frac{1}{2 \pi f X_C}\\ &=\frac{1}{2 \pi \times 50 \times 66.36}\\ &=47.96 \mu F \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **48** (acceptable range: [47, 49]).

ee:2016:q41.title: GATE EE 2016 | Set 1 | Question: 41
ee:2016:q41.question:
A 30 MVA, 3-phase, 50 Hz, 13.8 kV, star-connected synchronous generator has positive, negative and zero sequence reactances, 15%, 15% and 5% respectively. A reactance ($X_n$) is connected between the neutral of the generator and ground. A double line to ground fault takes place involving phases 'b' and 'c', with a fault impedance of j0.1 p.u. The value of $X_n$ (in p.u.) that will
limit the positive sequence generator current to 4270 A is _________.

detailed_solution.markdown:
Base current,

$$\begin{aligned} I_B&=\frac{30 \times 10^3}{\sqrt{3} \times 13.8}=1255.109A\\ I_f&=4270A\\ I_{p.u.}&=\frac{4270}{1255.109}=3.402p.u.\\ I_{g1}&=\frac{E_a}{X_1+(X_2||X_0)}\\ &\text{where, }\\ X_0&=X_0+3(Z_n+Z_f)\\ X_0&=3Z_n+0.35\\ 3.402&=\frac{1.0}{0.15+\frac{0.15 \times (3Z_n+0.35)}{0.15+3Z_n+0.35}}\\ &\text{Solving the equation,}\\ Z_n&=1.07 \;p.u. \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **1.1** (acceptable range: [1.05, 1.15]).

ee:2016:q44.title: GATE EE 2016 | Set 1 | Question: 44
ee:2016:q44.question: The switches T1 and T2 in Figure (a) are switched in a complementary fashion with sinusoidal pulse width modulation technique. The peak value of the 100 Hz component of the load current ($i_{L}$), in ampere, is ________ .

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} m_a&=0.8\\ (V_{01})_{peak}&=m_a\frac{V_d}{2}\;\;[m_a\leq 1]\\ &=0.8 \times 250=200V\\ (I_{01})_{peak}&=\frac{(V_{01})_{peak}}{Z_1}\\ &=\frac{200}{\sqrt{R^2}+(\omega L)^2}\\ &=\frac{200}{\sqrt{12^2+16^2}}=10A \end{aligned}$$

ee:2016:q45.title: GATE EE 2016 | Set 1 | Question: 45
ee:2016:q45.question: The voltage ($v_{s}$) across and the current ($i_{s}$) through a semiconductor switch during a turn-ON transition are shown in figure. The energy dissipated during the turn-ON transition, in mJ, is _______.

primary.subtopicLabel: Power Semiconductor Devices and Commutation Techniques

detailed_solution.concept: Power Electronics - Power Semiconductor Devices and Commutation Techniques
detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Energy}&=\int_{0}^{T_1}V\cdot i dt+\int_{0}^{T_2}V\cdot i dt\\ &=V\left [ \frac{1}{2}IT_1 \right ]+I\left [ \frac{1}{2}VT_2 \right ]\\ &=600\left [ \frac{150}{2}\times 1 \times 10^{-6} \right ]\\ &+100\left [ \frac{1}{2} \times 600 \times 1 \times 10^{-6} \right ]\\ \text{ Energy}&=75mJ \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **75** (acceptable range: [74, 76]).

ee:2016:q46.title: GATE EE 2016 | Set 1 | Question: 46
ee:2016:q46.question: A single-phase 400 V, 50 Hz transformer has an iron loss of 5000 W at the rated condition. When operated at 200 V, 25 Hz, the iron loss is 2000 W. When operated at 416 V, 52 Hz, the value of the hysteresis loss divided by the eddy current loss is ______.

detailed_solution.markdown:
400V, 50Hz transformer, $P_i=5000Watt$

When,

200V, 25Hz,

$P_i=2000 Watt$

416V, 52Hz,  $\frac{P_h}{P_e}=?$

$$\begin{aligned} P_i &=P_h+P_e \\ P_h & \propto f B_m^x \\ P_e& \propto f^2B_m^2 \end{aligned}$$

as in the problem

$$\begin{aligned} \frac{V}{f}&=\frac{400}{50}=\frac{416}{52}=8 \\ P_h&=Af \\ P_e&=Bf^2 \end{aligned}$$

From given data,

$$\begin{aligned} 2000 &=(P_{25hZ})){i} \\ &= A(25)+B(25)^2\;\;...(i)\\ 5000 &=(P_{50Hz})_i \\ &= A(50)+B(50)^2\;\;...(ii) \end{aligned}$$

Solving equation (i) and (ii),

$$\begin{aligned} A &=60,\;\; B=0.8 \\ (P_h)_{52Hz}&=Af=60 \times 52 \\ &= 3120 Watt\\ (P_e)_{52Hz}&=Bf^2=0.8 \times (52)^2 \\ &= 2163.2 Watt\\ \frac{(P_h)_{52Hz}}{(P_e)_{52Hz}}&=\frac{3120}{2163.2}=1.4423 \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **1.45** (acceptable range: [1.4, 1.5]).

ee:2016:q47.title: GATE EE 2016 | Set 1 | Question: 47
ee:2016:q47.question:
A DC shunt generator delivers 45 A at a terminal voltage of 220 V. The armature and the shunt
field resistances are 0.01 $\Omega$ and 44 $\Omega$ respectively. The stray losses are 375 W. The percentage efficiency of the DC generator is ____________.

detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} \text{Stay losses} &= 375 \; \text{Watt}\\ & \text{Total copper losses}\\ &= I_a^2R_a+I_{sh}^2R_{sh}\\ &= 50^2 \times (0.01)+(5^2)\times 44\\ &= 1125\; \text{Watt}\\ h &=\frac{\text{Output}}{\text{Output}+\text{losses}} \\ &= \frac{220 \times 45}{220 \times 45+(1125)+375}\\ &= 0.86842 \;\text{or} \; 86.84\% \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **87** (acceptable range: [86, 88]).

ee:2016:q48.title: GATE EE 2016 | Set 1 | Question: 48
ee:2016:q48.question: A three-phase, 50 Hz salient-pole synchronous motor has a per-phase direct-axis reactance ($X_{d}$) of 0.8 pu and a per-phase quadrature-axis reactance ($X_{q}$) of 0.6 pu. Resistance of the machine is negligible. It is drawing full-load current at 0.8 pf (leading). When the terminal voltage is 1 pu, per-phase induced voltage, in pu, is _________.

detailed_solution.markdown:
Synchronous motor at leading p.f.

$$\begin{aligned} X_d &=0.8 \\ \phi &= 36.86\\ X_q&= 0.6\\ R_q&= 0\\ \tan \psi &=\frac{V \sin \phi +I_aX_a}{V \cos \phi }\\ \psi &=56.30 \end{aligned}$$

For synchronous motor at leading p.f.

$$\begin{aligned} \psi &=\phi +\delta \\ \delta &=19.70^{\circ} \\ E&=V \cos \delta +I_dX_d \\ I_d&=I_a \sin f=0.831 \\ E&=(1)\cos (19.7)+(0.831)(0.8) \\ &=1.606 \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **1.6** (acceptable range: [1.58, 1.62]).

ee:2016:q50.question: A single-phase full-bridge voltage source inverter (VSI) is fed from a 300 V battery. A pulse of 120$^{\circ}$ duration is used to trigger the appropriate devices in each half-cycle. The rms value of the fundamental component of the output voltage, in volts, is

ee:2016:q51.title: GATE EE 2016 | Set 1 | Question: 51
ee:2016:q51.question: A single-phase transmission line has two conductors each of 10 mm radius. These are fixed at a center-to-center distance of 1 m in a horizontal plane. This is now converted to a three-phase transmission line by introducing a third conductor of the same radius. This conductor is fixed at an equal distance D from the two single-phase conductors. The three-phase line is fully transposed. The positive sequence inductance per phase of the three-phase system is to be 5% more than that of the inductance per conductor of the single-phase system. The distance D, in meters, is _______.

detailed_solution.markdown: In first case, $$\begin{aligned} L_1&=2 \times 10^{-7} \ln \frac{D}{r}\\ &=2 \times 10^{-7} \ln \left ( \frac{100}{0.7788} \right )\\ &=0.97\mu H/m\\ L_2&=1.05 \times 0.97=1.0185 \mu H/m\\ L_2&=2 \times 10^{-7} \ln \left ( \frac{\sqrt[3]{D^2 \times 100}}{0.7788} \right ) \end{aligned}$$ $$\begin{aligned} \ln \left ( \frac{\sqrt[3]{D^2 \times 100}}{0.7788} \right )&=\frac{1.0185 \times 10^{-6}}{2 \times 10^{-7}}\\ &=5.0925\\ e^{5.0925}&= \frac{\sqrt[3]{D^2 \times 100}}{0.7788} \\ D&=142.7cm=1.427m \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **1.44** (acceptable range: [1.41, 1.47]).

ee:2016:q55.question: In the circuit shown below, the node voltage In the circuit shown below, the node voltage $V_{A}$ is ___________ V.

detailed_solution.concept: Electric Circuits - Basics of Electric Circuit
detailed_solution.markdown: Applying KCL at node A, we get $\frac{V_A}{5}+\frac{V_A-10}{10}+\frac{V_A+10I_1}{5}=5$ So, $2V_A+V_A-10+2V_A+20I_1=5$ $5V_A+20I_1=60$ Since, $I_1=\frac{V_A-10}{10}$ So, $5V_A+2V_A-20=60$ $7V_A=80$ $V_A=11.42 volt$ Therefore, the correct answer is **11.375** (acceptable range: [11.25, 11.5]).
